title: VPC install preflight and escalation log — Mar 2026
body:
Context:
- Purpose: rolling notes from the VPC/on-prem preflight for Acme Health (PHI scope). Primary goal is to capture surface-level install issues, escalations, and immediate action items before the formal runbook update. This doc intended for SRE/Platform/Eng leads to triage.
- Install window: 2026-03-22 -> 2026-03-25 (on-site techs + remote eng support).

Attendees (remote + on-site):
- Priya Nair (install lead)
- Ethan Martinez (SRE)
- Lina Zhou (platform eng)
- Omar Rahman (solutions eng, on-site)
- Sofia Petrov (security/compliance)
- Acme on-site: Danika (netops), Miguel (storage)

Summary snapshot (high level):
- Preflight uncovered three class A issues that required escalation: GPU driver/kernel mismatch, outbound KMS egress policy ambiguity, and intermittent NFS timeouts under parallel snapshot load.
- Two quick wins completed during window: added missing NTP cron on nodes and white-listing of internal metrics egress to Prometheus endpoint.
- Remaining: formalizing a firewall rule template and adding a transient PVC size recommendation to the runbook.

Daily log / notable items:
2026-03-22 
- Kickoff, validate hardware list vs inventory. Found one rack with mixed GPU types (A100 + A10s) not in the order. Decision: isolate A10s to a separate node pool; do not provision them for production workload.
- Action: Ethan to produce node-pool labeling script by 2026-03-25.

2026-03-23 
- First full cluster bring-up. Several pods crashlooping with CUDA initialization errors. Root cause: host installed NVIDIA driver 525.x while our runtime expects 535.x (CUDA 12 ABI mismatch).
- Mitigation: rolled back to container runtime that bundles 525-compatible kernels for customer QA environment; escalated to infra team to schedule host driver update in maintenance window.
- Notes-to-self: update preflight checklist to explicitly require driver version 535+ for any cluster running model-serving 1.8+.

2026-03-24 
- KMS access: Acme's security team unsure if outbound to our KMS endpoint over TLS 1.3 on port 443 meets their policy since they enforce egress constraints by service FQDN instead of IP.
- Escalation: product-security + legal consulted; decided to add an optional HSM-on-prem connector doc and provide signed TLS cert fingerprint for egress allowlist.
- Action: Sofia to draft HSM connector FAQ and KMS fingerprint file by 2026-03-27.

2026-03-25 
- Storage: parallel VM-level snapshot job caused short NFS stalls (~300-800ms) when multiple inference nodes flushed logs. Observed increased p99 latency on model endpoints during snapshot window.
- Temporary mitigation: move snapshot window off-peak. Long-term: recommend increasing NFS export thread count and provide an alternates section in runbook for customers with >3 inference nodes.
- Action: Omar to coordinate with Miguel (Acme storage) to capture iostat and export config; due 2026-03-30.

Decisions made:
- No mixing of mixed-generation GPUs in a single pool for production. Must use node_pools labels and taints.
- Driver version requirement: host NVIDIA driver >= 535. Container images will keep vendor-compatible toolkits as fallback in non-prod.
- For customers that restrict egress by IP, we will provide a signed cert fingerprint + optional on-prem HSM connector (docs + support path).

Action items (quick list):
- Ethan: node-pool labeling script + docs (due 2026-03-25)
- Sofia: HSM connector FAQ + KMS fingerprint bundle (due 2026-03-27)
- Omar: collect NFS metrics and export config with Acme storage lead (due 2026-03-30)
- Priya: update preflight checklist with driver/kernel, NTP, ephemeral PVC sizing heuristics (due 2026-03-28)
- Lina: create firewall-template snippet (ingress/egress port list) for runbook (due 2026-03-29)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we support mixed-GPU clusters in a single control plane with explicit node selectors, or prohibit by policy? (ops cost vs customer needs).
- For customers that require air-gapped HSM, what's the supported fallback for KMS rotation automation? Need product input.

Runbook notes (to fold into existing runbook):
- Add explicit host prerequisites: kernel >= 5.15, nvidia-driver >= 535, containerd 1.7+, iptables-nft compatibility.
- NTP: require chronyd or systemd-timesyncd with config snippet; add a cron check that alerts if drift > 500ms.
- Networking: recommended firewall rules (egress): 443 to kms.redwood.ai, 443 to metrics.redwood.ai, 9411 for tracing (optional). Provide FQDN + cert fingerprint for allowlist cases.
- Storage: recommend NFS server config with async disabled for active workloads and a suggested snapshot window off-peak. Include iops guidance per inference node.

Escalation log (who contacted + time):
- 2026-03-23 15:12 UTC -> Infra team pager for driver mismatch (contact: Ethan).
- 2026-03-24 09:30 UTC -> Product-security Slack + legal, re: KMS egress (contact: Sofia).
- 2026-03-25 17:02 UTC -> Solutions-eng escalation to Customer-Eng for snapshot impact (contact: Omar).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider shipping a lightweight preflight agent that validates kernel/driver/runtime and produces a single telemetry report to attach to customer ticket. Would save ~30-60m per install.
- Add a short 'troubleshooting cheat sheet' for on-site techs: top 5 checks (NTP, drivers, DNS, firewall, storage perf).

Immediate followups for next sync (2026-03-29):
- Walkthrough of updated runbook sections (Priya + Lina).
- Demo of node-pool labeling script (Ethan).
- HSM FAQ review (Sofia).

Appendix (links and refs):
- Quick driver reference: nvidia.com/driver-table (internal note: pin to 535+ in runbook)
- Related jira: PD-3421 (install failure - driver mismatch)
- Infra PR: #512 fixes container runtime fallback behavior

End.
